An Exceptional Private Education in London
Chepstow House School is a premium independent school in Notting Hill that offers world-class private education at the nursery and prep stages, empowering pupils to maximise their potential in school and beyond.
Experienced teachers with the best credentials guide learners through a challenging, carefully crafted curriculum, enhanced by cutting-edge facilities. Pupils become academically accomplished, achieve top outcomes and progress to the most prestigious day and boarding schools.
Our expansive extracurricular programme fosters children’s unique talents in exciting areas, along with the skills to succeed in later life.
Why Choose Our School in Notting Hill?
Our exceptional academic provision at Chepstow House School, and well-rounded approach to pastoral care, equips children with the skills, knowledge and confidence they need to excel both in the classroom and beyond. Our outstanding results speak for themselves with our children receiving coveted offers to top London day schools and prestigious boarding schools.
At our private school in Notting Hill, London, dedicated subject specialist teachers use innovative techniques and the latest insights to nurture critical thinking, creativity and excellence across a broad range of disciplines, including languages, science, sports, music, art and drama. Here, we lay the foundation for lifelong success, helping every child unlock their full potential and thrive in an ever-evolving world.

Inspiring, skilled teachers who deliver outstanding results.
Prestigious School Destinations
Our graduates transition to top senior schools in London and the UK.
Promoting All-Rounded Excellence

As an Inspired School, Chepstow House School and Little Chepstow Nursery offer world-class private education with the aim of providing our children with the best start to their school career possible. Inspired pupils access top teaching provision, achieve excellent results in national and international curricula, and regularly attend their first-choice university.
In championing all-rounded development, our private school in Notting Hill mirrors Inspired’s commitment to promoting achievement in three key areas – namely, Academics, Sports, and Performing and Creative Arts. Our children go on to become academically accomplished, multi-skilled individuals with countless opportunities awaiting them in school and later life.

Access to a Global Group of Premium Schools
Access to a Global Group of Premium Schools
Inspired is a global group of 110+ premium private schools, united by their mission of delivering an exceptional education. To date, 85,000+ students are enrolled in Inspired schools across 24 countries and comprise a diverse community for fostering lifelong friendships and connections.
Dedicated Personalised Teaching
Dedicated Personalised Teaching
Inspired is proud to employ talented educators who are committed to exceptional private education provision and possess the skills needed to unlock students’ full potential. By adopting a personalised approach to learning, our teachers provide one of the best school experiences, helping students achieve their personal objectives and foster a love of learning that extends far into the future.
Exclusive Summer Camps and Exchange Programme
Exclusive Summer Camps and Exchange Programme
Inspired's global community of premium private schools offers thrilling opportunities for travel and connecting with students worldwide. By participating in themed summer camps and student exchange programs, Chepstow House students build lasting friendships, develop learning networks and broaden their outlooks through immersion in other cultures.
As a member of Inspired Education, our school in Notting Hill employs subject specialists with outstanding credentials to help guide students through our broad and challenging curriculum. They are experts with a deep understanding which they use to deliver leading private education provision, and take pleasure in challenging students to explore and cultivate their specific interests. Specialist subjects at our school include Languages, Science, Sports, Music, Art and Drama.
Hear From our Community
I wanted to join Chepstow House School because my brother leaves school every day with a smile on his face.
The School embraces the individual – teachers don’t teach the cohort, they teach the child.

About Us
A Word from Our Head
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to our school’s website. As Head of Chepstow House, I am proud to lead a community that values each and every member, whether they are a child, parent or staff.
Our school is built upon a family community ethos, in which everyone is welcomed, respected and encouraged to grow. We believe in fostering a supportive and nurturing environment, where children can develop their academic, social and emotional skills, and reach their full potential.
At Chepstow House, we strive for sustainable learning. Students are taught to think critically and creatively about the world around them. We are committed to providing a curriculum that is both challenging and engaging, preparing our children for a successful future beyond the classroom.
We are also proud to deliver fantastic results for our students’ transition into senior school. Our children are well-prepared for the next stage of their academic journey, and we are delighted to see them go on to excel at a wide variety of London day and boarding schools.
However, we recognise that academic achievement is not the only measure of success. We place a strong emphasis on the wellbeing of individual children, helping them to develop their self-esteem, resilience and emotional intelligence. We believe that a happy and healthy child is better equipped to succeed in all areas of their life.
At Chepstow House, we understand the importance of parents in the education of their children, recognising that a strong partnership between home and school is essential for supporting student learning and wellbeing.
Thank you for considering Chepstow House as a place of learning for your child. I invite you to explore our website further and discover the unique qualities that make our school community so special.
Angela Barr, Head Teacher
A Pathway to Success
Chepstow House aims to create a happy, sustainable learning environment, in which children develop resilience and perseverance. Our school is a centre of learning excellence where children can develop as well-rounded individuals, while interacting with and growing as part of a community that promotes a spirit of collaboration, collective accountability and responsibility.
A History of Exceptional Education Provision
Chepstow House opened at 19 Pembridge Villas, Notting Hill. Twenty-four pupils joined in Reception and began their transformative journey at our school.
The school moved to its present location after outgrowing its original premises. Little Chepstow Nursery opened, allowing us to accommodate 2 to 11-year-olds at our magnificent school.
The first year 6 cohort graduated. A testament to our excellence, they achieved outstanding 11+ results and secured entry into top London day and boarding schools.
With 10 years of experience in excellent education provision, Chepstow House was firmly established as a top London co-ed school.
Chepstow House joined Inspired Education, a leading global group of 110+ private schools, increasing opportunities for our pupils inside class and out.
A Holistic, Flexible and Inspiring Curriculum
Our exceptional curriculum offers a secure and imaginative basis for academic success between Reception and year 6. At Chepstow House, we encourage children to become positive, responsible individuals, who can work and cooperate with others while developing the skills and knowledge needed to reach their full potential.
With the support of our subject specialists, our children receive excellent outcomes, and achieve their goals and aspirations in and out of the classroom. Our subject specialists are essential in helping pupils find and cultivate their specific talents and interests, and by sharing their passion for the subject, our dedicated teachers deliver lessons that are challenging and inspirational. Small class sizes and support staff help to maximise assimilation across learning areas.
Discover more about our magnificent school and how an ambitious, all-rounded education can help your child to unlock their true potential at Chepstow House.

Specialist Subjects
Expert Guidance for Outstanding Results
At Chepstow House, we have trained subject specialists who enjoy challenging children and developing their abilities across learning areas. Our specialists aim to promote critical thinking and foster a diverse skill set that includes the tools for success in school and beyond. Expert tuition allows children to achieve highly in academics while also inspiring them to pursue their unique interests. By cultivating their curiosity and a love of learning, children emerge confident, responsible and engaged citizens, capable of making a positive impact on the world.
The Art Department is an exciting, vibrant hub where children can explore their creativity. In addition, children can participate in a range of enriching activities that build confidence and provide vital exposure to the industry at a professional level.
Art features strongly in the curriculum as well as in extracurricular activities. Children receive weekly art lessons from a specialist teacher from reception to year 6; they develop a visual art sketchbook while learning that art is both a process and an outcome. For those with an interest in developing their skills further, we offer art clubs for both Key Stages, taught by internal staff and external providers Creativityarts. We also celebrate the works of our children with a revolving display throughout the premises. In addition to brightening our school environment, this helps to instil pride in one’s own accomplishments.
Opportunities for learning are not limited to the classroom. Gallery trips, workshops and art competitions are a regular feature in the life of the Art Department. Chepstow House exhibited in the National Gallery’s Take One Picture Exhibition (a combined project with our Science Department) in 2019/20, and entered the Mayor of London’s Fourth Plinth competition and the Royal Academy of Art: Young Artist Competition. Year 3 also participated in Tate Britain and Steve McQueen’s ambitious collaboration project. In addition, we support the Royal College of Art: Young Art Competition and the amazing charitable work thereof.
Miss Luke has a fine art background with a specialism in curation. Her experience includes working with galleries and art-based charities curating and organising exhibitions in and around London. Miss Luke aims to offer all children the chance to explore and express themselves through a wide range of creative media, and to establish an understanding of the subject through both practical and theoretical understanding.
Our diverse sport offering helps children to become active, healthy and physically fit while equipping them with critical personal qualities. Our Sports Department includes qualified staff who are dedicated to providing a fun learning environment and encourage enjoyment of physical exercise; as a result, children are likelier to develop a strong self-esteem, and gain confidence and effective communication skills, while crucially improving their unique sporting abilities.
Children in Reception to year 2 learn the fundamental concepts and basic principles of Physical Education (PE) across a variety of sports. All the children have three lessons a week, including: dance, football and netball in autumn; hockey, rugby and gymnastics in spring; and cricket, athletics and rounders in summer. They also receive one term of swimming lessons at Kensington Leisure Centre nearby. The year concludes with an exciting sports day at which children proudly showcase their many talents to their family and friends.
In years 3 to 6, the children receive two lessons a week from the Sports Department, the focus of which is on gender-neutral sports in a co-ed environment. During the week, children have one PE lesson for an individual/artistic sport, such as dance, gymnastics, athletics and tennis. On Fridays, they have a games lesson when they go off site to practise football, hockey, netball, rugby, athletics and cricket. For half of the school year, learners receive structured swimming lessons on a weekly basis at the Kensington Leisure Centre. We teach the importance of gamesmanship and sportsmanship from an early age. Competitive fixtures and tournaments against other local prep schools take place weekly and include multiple teams so that all children can participate and enjoy these vital experiences.
A rich programme of extracurricular activities and events supplements these sessions and gives learners the opportunity to gain new experiences and pursue personal interests. Opportunities include termly tournaments, international tours and inter-house netball, rugby, football and cross-country, among others. For more details, we also invite you to explore our Extracurricular Activities.
Music plays an important part in the life of Chepstow House. Our exemplary curriculum, instrumental programme and extracurriculars provide children with a solid basis in music and a path to success as future professional musicians. In addition, pupils gain confidence through opportunities to display their musical abilities, including school assemblies, concerts, end-of-term productions and class performances. Each child from reception to year 6 learns music as a classroom subject, which is taught by a specialist teacher and develops their knowledge and skills in three main areas: listening and appraising, performing and composing. Our syllabus covers pitch, rhythm and notation too, helping children to establish a sound understanding of both theory and practice.
Children with significant talent or an interest in specific instruments or fields of music benefit from specialised lessons in addition to classroom music from year 1 onwards. Specialist educators, all of whom are experienced teachers and performers, enjoy challenging and guiding students in a range of vocal and instrumental lessons. As such, students hone their abilities and gain valuable experience in their chosen discipline, be it singing, piano, violin, cello, flute, clarinet, saxophone, guitar, ukulele, drums or brass instruments. Lessons take place during regular school hours on rotation, ensuring that students never miss the same lesson week to week. Our pupils also have the opportunity to participate in the following choirs and instrumental ensembles: KS1 Choir, KS2 Choir, Trumpet Club, Guitar/Uke Ensemble and Rock Band.
Ms Darkins is an experienced musician, performer and teacher. Her first love is the flute, and she has also studied piano, oboe, conducting and music theory. She studied for her BA in music and French at the University of Southampton and later completed her PGCE at Roehampton. As a flautist, she studied with several leaders in the field, including Trevor Wye and Paul Edmund Davies. She has extensive performance experience and has won many competitions and prizes. Ms Darkins is a seasoned conductor and music leader, having taught in both primary and secondary schools. She is passionate about engaging children in a lifelong love of music. As such, she has designed a curriculum that is accessible, meaningful and fun, building the children’s confidence through performance and preparing them for opportunities in the modern music industry by introducing them not only to Mozart and Beethoven but also film music, GarageBand and the diversity of musical traditions from around the world.
At Chepstow House, French sits at the heart of a dynamic and carefully crafted language curriculum. Our engaging programme inspires curiosity and equips children with the skills and confidence to grow into capable, enthusiastic language learners.
Education in languages assists children in their understanding of the world’s diversity while contributing to the reinforcement of knowledge, skills and comprehension in other subjects.
Our children receive French lessons once a week from reception to year 6. These lessons offer a foundation on which pupils may develop their proficiency and confidence in the French language: as they progress, children acquire and utilise a growing bank of vocabulary, language skills and grammatical knowledge.
Cross-curricular activities assist children by providing an invaluable opportunity to extend their knowledge and apply skills across different subject areas in a meaningful and connected way. To complement lessons, children take home a weekly French home pack that includes bilingual books, illustrated French recipes, and a scrapbook to which they are encouraged to contribute with presentations on aspects of French and francophone culture.
Over 30 languages are spoken at Chepstow House by children and staff, creating a diverse school community that foster tolerance and an appreciation of other cultures. Each year, a Language Captain is elected to promote enthusiasm for languages across the school and to help create a positive, engaging environment where French is visible and valued by all pupils.
Positive curiosity and a genuine interest in foreign languages are integral to the syllabus which seeks to inspire and excite pupils using a range of themes and topics. Language Angels is the scheme of work used throughout the school, which children can also access at home to deepen their language knowledge.
MADAME ROBINNE – French Teacher
Madame Robinne, a native French speaker from Versailles, began teaching French in primary schools in 2005, after working in Paris and London as a lawyer in the aviation and space insurance sector. She joined Chepstow House when it first opened in January 2010 and developed our engaging and progressive French curriculum for Reception to year 6, as the school expanded.
Through the use of performance, the Drama Department aims to instil confidence in every child and help them to tap into their creativity and flair. Every year group takes part in their own performance of either existing productions or original pieces written by the staff. Our extracurricular clubs offer children additional opportunities to pursue an interest and develop their skills in the performing arts, including after-school drama lessons and tuition from the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA). Some of our recent performances include The Nativity, The Future-Proof Zoo, A Butterfly Named Maia, Oliver!, Pandora’s Box, The Lion King and Cinderfella.
Our enjoyable Science curriculum stimulates interest in the process of scientific enquiry and prepares children for the rigorous academic demands of the common entrance exams.
Children receive Science lessons from their class teachers in reception to year 2 and learn in a well-equipped laboratory from year 3 onwards. By prioritising hands-on exploration, we equip learners with crucial experimental and investigative skills. Critical thinking is essential as pupils begin to evaluate scientific evidence and develop ideas. Classes teach learners how to utilise their knowledge to communicate their ideas to each other and explain various phenomena in the world around them. In addition, children examine the impact of new technologies and human behaviour on the environment.
Chepstow House gives students the opportunity to explore science outside of school, including visits to the Royal Society Summer Exhibition, The Old Operating Theatre and the Royal Observatory Greenwich. Each year, we celebrate science with Science Week, which coincides with British Science Week: The whole school undertakes a variety of investigations, with the older students supporting the younger ones. Owing to Chepstow House’s strong connections with top independent schools nationwide, such as Dulwich College and Stowe School, our pupils enjoy many opportunities to engage in scientific education in other learning environments.
After completing his bachelor's in human biology at Loughborough University, Mr Buckley received a PGCE from the University of Sussex. He taught in secondary schools across East Sussex before going back to university to study for a master's at UWL and has since been self-employed as an international private tutor. Mr Buckley enjoys drawing from his many experiences to create an exciting, stimulating learning environment and foster a passion for science in his students.
Learn more about the specialist subjects that we offer and how our trained, motivated teachers can help your child achieve excellence across learning areas.

Parent Community
Friends of Chepstow House
At Chepstow House, we recognise that parents and guardians are an integral part of every child's schooling and that is why we have Friends of Chepstow House (FCH). This dedicated parent-teacher association serves as the bridge between staff and parents, as well as with chosen charities and the local community. Throughout the year, FCH organises and runs events aimed at children and adults. These include seasonal celebrations, a variety of fundraising galas, second-hand sales to support our selected charities, and other activities.
FCH consists of an executive committee and class reps, whose role is essential in fostering a strong, happy parent community. Class reps act as the link between teachers and parents as well as hosting social events, such as regular coffee mornings and cocktail evenings.
The governing ethos of FCH is to increase involvement, whether large or small, and to encourage as many parents and guardians as possible to participate in the fun opportunities and events that take place throughout the year. We warmly invite parents and guardians to join in with the activities of FCH.
Discover more about FCH and how your child can benefit from joining our friendly, supportive school community.

Scholarships & Bursaries
Coming to learn at Chepstow House is an extraordinary experience, which has shaped and transformed the lives of many boys and girls over the years. Not only are we proud to provide excellent learning opportunities, but we aim to extend these opportunities to deserving candidates who lack the resources to enrol in Chepstow House. By offering financial support to students from different backgrounds, our school fosters an inclusive environment that is highly engaging and rich in potential learning experiences.
A Pathway to Success for Deserving Candidates
We provide bursaries to deserving candidates wishing to enrol in Year 4 (i.e., at the age of 9+) at Chepstow House, with a view to preparing for the 11+ entrance exams. All applications are fully means tested, both initially and on an annual basis.
Our partner charity, the Gold Standard Charitable Trust (GSCT), is responsible for raising funds for all Inspired UK Schools. Each year, GSCT supports parents of talented pupils who lack the resources to obtain an exceptional education. GSCT Trustees will review the circumstances, including the financial status, of each family that applies for a bursary before making a final decision.
How to Apply for a Bursary
To begin the process of unlocking your child's full potential with a transformative education at Chepstow House, apply for a bursary using the button below.
Nsouli Scholars
A Transformative Opportunity
The Nsouli Scholars Programme is an exciting global initiative that promises to transform lives by enabling 50 extraordinary students at any one time to attend any of Inspired’s prestigious schools on a full scholarship for the duration of their education. The ambition is that the scholarship will provide hundreds of children with an opportunity to receive a truly transformative education.
By opening this path to exceptional individuals, we hope to expand our community, and to empower children of all backgrounds with unrivalled opportunities in academics, sports, the arts and extracurricular activities. In this sense, the Nsouli Scholars Programme is an investment both in education and in shaping the leaders of tomorrow.
This generous endowment honours Nadim Nsouli, who founded Inspired in 2013 as a definitive statement of excellence in private international education. In recognition of Mr Nsouli’s Lebanese heritage and Inspired’s commitment to inclusivity, several scholarships will be awarded to individuals of Lebanese origin.
Inspired schools offer a world-class educational experience that combines academics and engaging extra-curricular activities, producing confident, multi-skilled students who flourish in a competitive and increasingly interconnected world. Along with expert instruction by hand-picked teachers, our students access specialist sports programmes and professional tutelage from leaders in the performing and creative arts. As a result, they leave armed with a robust value system and a love of learning that extends well beyond the classroom.
Inspired is also committed to leveraging new and transformative learning technologies. Inspired AI empowers children to achieve academic excellence by delivering actionable insights that are unique to each student, including strengths and weaknesses. Our partnership with The Royal College of Music and Forte, a revolutionary online platform, enables children to receive personalised music tuition from professionals. Students with musical interests benefit from bespoke private lessons, advancing their practice as creatives and gaining valuable performance experience.
The advantages of our holistic approach to education are evidenced by the fact that Inspired students consistently excel in academic performance, surpassing national and global averages. In 2022, the Average Point Score was 35 for those undertaking the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma, for which the world average was 31.98, while A* scores comprised 27% of our students' A Level grades, compared to 14.6% globally. As a consequence, many are able to attend leading universities, with one in three graduates going on to a Russell Group University or Ivy League College.
The Inspired Group includes top-rated day and boarding schools worldwide, meaning students enjoy access to a diverse international community. Be it through specialised Summer Camps or immersive Global Exchange Programmes, children have the chance to travel broadly and engage meaningfully with different cultures, meet and learn from our esteemed partners, build lifelong networks, and become more independent.
Discover more about bursaries for our magnificent school. Our friendly team will be happy to answer any questions you may have.

pageCache.text:
Nursery in Notting Hill
An Exceptional Preschool Education in Notting Hill
At our private co-ed nursery in Notting Hill, London, we empower children to unlock their full potential through exploratory play, an exciting and multi-faceted curriculum, and a caring and stimulating learning environment. With expert guidance from our skilled teachers, children are challenged to develop key competencies, including language and emotional and social skills, ensuring a smooth transition when the time comes to move to preparatory school.
Nursery is a critical stage in a child’s education where they are developing their unique character, and gaining valuable life skills. During this stage it is also important to establish a foundation for academic success, and to allow time to discover new talents that can be developed at school and beyond. With excellent teaching and a wide range of resources, we prepare children for unlimited future accomplishments. Throughout their time at Little Chepstow Nursery, children explore meaningful learning experiences and develop the literacy and numeracy skills necessary for the next stage of their educational journey.
Little Chepstow Nursery in Notting Hill offers morning and full-day sessions for children aged 2 to 4.
Why Choose Our Nursery in Notting Hill, London?
Upon joining our Notting Hill nursery, children explore a diverse syllabus, with engaging activities that support them to learn and develop each day. Our preschool curriculum is carefully planned to promote confidence, resilience and autonomy, as well as growth across key areas, from literacy to mathematics, physical activity, and expressive art and design.
We treat every child as an individual and cultivate their unique interests, passions and talents from a young age. Our skilled and passionate pre-prep staff support children as they enjoy learning through structured lessons, play and exploration.
To further enhance learning and development, we engage closely with our parent community, ensuring they are actively and enthusiastically involved in their child's preschool education. As pupils advance through our Notting Hill pre-prep school, parents can monitor their progress using Arc Pathway; this cutting-edge educational platform allows parents to maximise their child’s learning potential by making informed decisions based on their needs.
At our private nursery in Notting Hill, we prepare children to excel in their preschool years while also establishing a firm foundation for a life of learning and achievement.
Nursery Options
Little Chepstow is a sessional nursery in Notting Hill that offers both morning sessions and full days. We offer up to five full days. Children can do full days in the term when they are ready.
Morning sessions: 8:45am to 11:50am Full days: 8:45am to 3:00pm
Our Nursery Curriculum
Our early education programme is meticulously crafted to promote key areas of children's development, all of which are equally important and interconnected.
Communication and language feature prominently to help children become effective communicators, using language to solve problems, hold discussions and build relationships.
We also focus on physical development, including movement, control and coordination. Children learn the importance of physical activity and making healthy choices regarding food and exercise.
Personal, social and emotional development involves helping children to improve their social skills, manage their feelings, and form positive relationships with others.
Important literacy skills are developed at this stage, with young children starting to decode words using phonic knowledge, exhibit an interest in and recognise the written word, start forming letters, and engage in pre-writing and mark-making activities.
Mathematics-related activities aim to encourage problem-solving and teach children about space, shapes and measurements. These include counting quantities, ordering numbers, and sorting and recognising numbers.
To help them make sense of the world and their community, we provide various opportunities for pupils to explore, observe and discover more about themselves, their families, other people, places, technology and the environment.
Children are encouraged to play with and explore different media and materials, and express themselves through art, music, movement, dance, role-play, and design and technology.
An Engaging and Stimulating Preschool Environment
Our purpose-built nursery is the ideal setting for developing children's distinct characters. Upon entering our preschool classrooms, children are met with a dynamic, stimulating learning environment that successfully fosters their creativity, growth and natural curiosity.
State-of-the-art classrooms at our nursery in Notting Hill, London, are carefully designed to provide a secure, nurturing space in which children can cultivate their core competencies, positive personal qualities, and unique talents and abilities. Fully equipped with excellent resources, each area offers opportunities for our pupils to develop through structured lessons, play and exploration.
Beyond the classroom, children enjoy learning by exploring and navigating our outdoor spaces, such as the Wild Area. These spaces are critical in a holistic early years programme, as they promote exercise, sensory engagement and exploration, and an appreciation of the natural world.
Outstanding Facilities for Preschool Education
Our spacious nursery facilities are fully equipped to give children the best start to their education. Exceptional resources promote hands-on learning, both indoors and outdoors, and encourage learners to build confidence, resilience and independence in a nurturing environment.
Bright, airy classrooms at our nursery provide ample room to explore different learning activities in a stimulating setting. Our pupils enjoy access to a large outdoor play area, complete with a mud kitchen and gardening area, fostering their creativity and physical wellbeing as they learn in and explore the natural environment.
Our Motivated Nursery Teachers
At our private nursery in Notting Hill, we hand-pick educators who are fully committed to eliciting the very best from pupils. Our dedicated teachers work tirelessly to craft lessons that are fun and stimulating, and incorporate key areas of learning and development. They also forge close relationships with reception staff to ensure that our pupils move smoothly to the next stage of their education. Their passion is not only an inspiration to our little ones but also essential for providing exceptional tuition at every level.
Language Immersion at the Preschool Level
Children at our Notting Hill nursery benefit from a robust language immersion experience. As little ones advance through our early education programme, they develop into skilled communicators who use language to solve problems and build confidence in expressing themselves. Literacy lessons entrench learning of written language elements, as children begin forming letters and applying their phonic knowledge. By equipping our pupils with a linguistic foundation, we prepare them for a more rigorous curriculum, including French lessons, in reception and beyond.
With over 15 languages spoken among staff and students, our school offers a dynamic language environment in which children gain valuable skills for an increasingly interconnected world.
Activities at the Preschool Stage
From learning about maths using different senses to exploring media in art and design lessons, our private Notting Hill nursery offers plenty of engaging activities to inspire, challenge and support children in their development.

An Inspired School
Embracing Individuality, Preparing Leaders
Chepstow House is part of Inspired Education, a leading global group of 121 premium schools. With 95,000+ students across 6 continents, Inspired leverages its role as an education heavyweight to deliver best-in-class learning experiences and begin children’s journey to exceptional outcomes.
By re-evaluating traditional teaching methods, the Inspired group offers an ambitious approach that seeks to reflect current attitudes and equip students with the tools to flourish at a global level. Expert guidance and academic tuition lead students to achieve excellent results, and gain in-demand skills and qualities conducive to success in school, leading universities and beyond. A generous extracurricular offering is central to Inspired’s educational philosophy: all children are pushed to pursue personal interests, explore new ones and unlock their full potential, whether in class, onstage or on the sports field. They leave confident and armed with a diverse skill set, which promises unlimited opportunities for future accomplishment.
The Three Pillars of an Inspired Education
When children join an Inspired school, they benefit from a holistic educational model that is geared towards excellence both in class and beyond. Underlying an Inspired education are three Pillars which represent key areas of development: Academics, Sport, and Performing & Creative Arts. By integrating each area into the learning process, Chepstow House equips children with a diverse skillset that mirrors Inspired’s commitment to delivering an exceptional school experience.
Academics are the central Pillar of an Inspired education. Inspired students access widely respected curricula that foster a range of transferable skills and empower them to succeed wherever they choose to go in the world. Exceptional teaching and learning provision, supported by cutting-edge technologies, helps students to unlock their full potential: in addition to outstanding results, they gain vital personal qualities, such as confidence and self-discipline, and become lifelong learners who enjoy the independent exploration of knowledge.
Performing and Creative Arts
Performing and Creative Arts
Fostering a child’s innate creativity is key to an education at Inspired schools. Across the curriculum and in extracurriculars, students enjoy access to exciting opportunities which aim to encourage creative thinking and develop their artistic proficiency. They become confident in their own abilities as artists and learn valuable skills, such as teamwork, leadership and problem-solving, which they can utilise in other disciplines too. Inspired’s art-based summer camps provide learners with additional opportunities to build networks and hone their craft among students with similar interests from other countries.
Due to the numerous benefits of regular physical activity, Sport is one of the three Pillars of an Inspired education. Being active not only helps to improve children’s physical, social and emotional wellbeing; it also provides opportunities to become highly skilled sportspeople, through specialist training at Inspired schools, paving the way for success at school and later in life. By taking part in Inspired’s global summer camps, students develop their sporting abilities even further while learning from and building connections with students from across the world.
Inspired Schools Around the World
Discover more about Inspired’s philosophy and how it helps bring out the very best in our students.

Reception
A Solid Foundation for Future Excellence
Our inspiring Reception curriculum prepares pupils for the next stage of their education while sparking a genuine interest in a range of themes and topics. Supported by skilled, passionate educators, children advance through a diverse syllabus that challenges them to excel in key areas of their development. Upon leaving Reception, they emerge confident, ambitious, independent, and armed with a varied skill set and a foundation for future accomplishment.
Literacy
Our literacy programme equips students with the tools needed to establish connections between sounds and letters, and begin reading and writing. At Chepstow House, children enjoy access to a range of reading materials to ignite their interest at this early stage; these include books, poems and other written materials. They also learn cursive using the Kingston Style and follow a structured phonics programme using Jolly Phonics. For more information on Literacy please click here.
Maths
In Reception, mathematics helps children to develop and improve their proficiency in counting, using numbers, understanding and completing simple addition and subtraction problems, and describing shapes, spaces and measurements. We use Numicon to promote a multi-sensory approach to maths and provide children with a better understanding of numbers.
Language
Communication and Language
The aim of communication and language is to develop children’s confidence and ability in expressing themselves. Other important skills they learn include speaking and listening in a range of situations. Our students benefit from a rich language environment with many opportunities for improving these proficiencies.
Physical Development
Physical Development
Physical development is a core aspect of a child’s growth at this early stage. At Chepstow House, we provide many opportunities for young children to be active and interactive, and improve vital abilities like movement, control and coordination. Children also learn the importance of physical activity and how to make healthy choices regarding food.
PSHE
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education
Personal, social and emotional development involves helping children to gain a positive sense of themselves and others. In addition to developing their social skills, children learn to build positive relationships, respect others, and have confidence in their own abilities; and how to manage their feelings and behave appropriately in groups.
Understanding the World
Understanding the World
Understanding the world involves guiding children with opportunities that help them make sense of the physical world and their community. Children enjoy various opportunities to explore, observe and find out about people, places, technology and the environment.
Arts & Design
Expressive Arts and Design
Expressive arts and design provide children with valuable opportunities to explore and play with a range of media and materials. We encourage children to share their thoughts, ideas and feelings through various activities involving art, music, movement, dance, role-play, and design and technology.
Specialist Lessions
Specialist lessons supplement the core EYFS curriculum and aim to further development in the above areas. Children receive lessons each week at Reception level, including in Art, French, Music and Physical Education. For further information, please see our Specialist Subjects.
Digital Literacy
Digital Literacy & Computing
Our digital literacy programme equips children with the tools to efficiently utilise a range of modern technologies, preparing them for success in an increasingly interconnected society. In computing lessons and across the curriculum, we focus on nurturing functional skills that help students use technology for both education and entertainment. In Reception, we teach learners how to programme bee-bots and computer software, understand everyday uses of technology, and store and manipulate digital content. We place considerable emphasis on the safety of our students; for this reason, our students learn to practise vital e-safety skills, like knowing when to take breaks from digital consumption and when to consume content using traditional methods.
Discover more about our ambitious curriculum and how we aim to prepare all pupils for success in school and beyond.

Policies & Inspection Reports
ISI and Ofsted Reports
As a member of the Independent Association of Prep Schools (IAPS), Chepstow House is regularly inspected by the approved Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI). In January 2018, the Office for Standards in Education, Children's Services and Skills (Ofsted) declared Chepstow House "an outstanding school".
It is a requirement of the Independent Schools Regulation that parents are informed if there have been any complaints at the formal stage. There has been one formal complaint to date.

Extracurricular Activities
Stimulating Opportunities for Holistic Development
At Chepstow House, our children benefit from an extensive extracurricular programme, which aims to equip them with the most in-demand skills, from harnessing AI to critical thinking, problem-solving and advanced coding.
Pupils take full advantage of our rich club offering to discover and cultivate their unique interests and abilities, whether in art, drama, sport, music or computing. In conjunction with enriching residential trips, these activities foster diverse competencies and establish pathways to future opportunities, such as merit-based scholarships, as children gain valuable experience and build networks of like-minded individuals.
Ample outdoor areas at our campus accommodate all sports and physical education up until year 2. Offsite facilities are used from year 3 onwards, including full-sized courts and pitches, for the coaching of rugby, football, cricket, athletics, hockey and netball. Swimming takes place at Kensington Leisure Centre.
Residential Trips
Residential trips are a key part of a Chepstow House education, with exciting and unique learning opportunities for children outside the classroom. Starting in year 3, children embark on a thrilling trip suitable to their age group. Trips take place in the summer term and provide pupils with the chance to explore new interests and experiences, gain skills that benefit them now and in years to come, and enjoy bonding with their peers.
Year 3 students spend one night at Bushcraft. Children stay at ‘The Woods’ (Cornbury Park), living in the wild, sleeping under canvas and cooking over open fires. It is an unforgettable two days where they all form many happy memories.
In year 4, students visit Little Canada, Isle of Wight. During their three-night sojourn, children take part in a range of both land-based and water activities, including water skiing, climbing, abseiling, surfing and coastal exploration, developing their sense of responsibility, self-reliance and a heightened self-esteem. Children come away feeling more independent and with plenty of amazing stories to tell.
Students in year 5 have a four-night water sports trip to Rockley Park, Poole. The park has its own private beach where the children can sail, windsurf and kayak. It is an adventurous, fun-packed experience that every child enjoys participating in.
Year 6 students are treated to an immersive cultural trip, in which they travel abroad to Normandy, France. Here they have the opportunity to develop their French language skills, try different cuisines and immerse themselves the French way of life.
Clubs
From team sports to performing arts, our clubs aim to foster children's distinct talents and promote the discovery of new skills and passions. We believe each child is wonderfully unique, and this is reflected in the breadth of our club offering. Our rich programme empowers pupils with all manner of personal interests to excel in a fun, highly stimulating learning environment.

Key Stage 1 Curriculum
Exceptional Education Provision for Years 1 and 2
Years 1 and 2 follow a broad, balanced curriculum, designed to challenge and inspire pupils. With expert guidance from our skilled teachers, children explore subjects in the National Curriculum along with enriching activities that foster holistic development. Specialist lessons enhance the learning process by encouraging children to think deeply and critically, develop their knowledge across disciplines, and cultivate their unique interests.
Click the icons below to learn more.
Literacy
In years 1 and 2 at Chepstow House, students have many opportunities to develop the skills of effective communication during literacy lessons. The curriculum is both challenging and inspiring. Using various resources, we aim to improve children’s knowledge and mastery of core competencies, from speaking and listening to spelling, grammar, writing comprehension, handwriting, reading and comprehension. Proficiencies like these serve as a basis for achievement in other subject areas, as well as in later school years and university.
Literacy lessons feature a range of activities that focus on communicating with adults and peers, including listening and responding, building vocabulary and encouraging children to articulate their knowledge and feelings. Using Jolly Phonics, we help children to improve their phonetic knowledge and develop an excellent understanding of the field. We believe all children should develop a love of reading. Thus, we encourage them to draw on their phonic knowledge to decode words and participate in discussions about a variety of books. Based on our weekly text focus, children will plan, draft and produce their own texts by combining a range of literacy skills. They will also use Word Aware to build a rich vocabulary in all subjects, while learning to write in cursive using the Kingston script.
View Curriculum Document
Maths
In the Key Stage 1 mathematics curriculum, our students work on vital skills that will empower them to excel across subject areas and in the wider world. The syllabus builds on the concepts covered in Reception, using various exciting resources to develop a range of vital, broadly applicable proficiencies.
We spend significant time ensuring children grasp key principles and are ready for more challenging work as they progress through the school. These include number and place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, fractions, measurement, properties of shape, position and direction, and data handling. To encourage mathematical thinking and help children make links between principles, we also teach problem solving, and use written, practical and computer-based activities, including Numicon, to embed knowledge and support number understanding.
View Curriculum Document
Science
Science in Key Stage 1 is an exciting opportunity for children to learn practical skills and develop their curiosity in different areas. Our broad science curriculum uses various topics to teach children all about the world we live in and help them become knowledgeable on a range of subjects, including animals, living things and their habitats, everyday materials, plants and seasonal change. In this core subject, children grow confident in their use of scientific methods, from questioning and observation to identification, classification, performing simple tests, making predictions and reaching conclusions.
View Curriculum Document
Digital Literacy
Digital Literacy & Computing
Digital literacy at Chepstow House helps children to successfully utilise a range of technologies and unlock their potential in a modern, interconnected world. Throughout the school day and in dedicated computing lessons, children learn functional skills related to IT literacy, education and entertainment. In Key Stage 1, children learn to programme bee-bots and computer software, store and manipulate digital content, and understand how technology is used in everyday life. Children’s safety is of prime importance to us; for this reason, we develop children’s e-safety skills, including knowing when to have a digital detox or use traditional methods to consume content. We use Microsoft Teams and SharePoint to link work in class with homework and to celebrate achievements across the school.
View Curriculum Document
Humanities
Humanities at Chepstow House include two key areas, history and geography, which students learn about through fascinating cross-curricular themes and topics. In history, we encourage them to consider significant global or national events, from the Great Fire of London to the lives of noteworthy individuals. In geography, children use maps to learn about the world’s continents and oceans and the countries that comprise the United Kingdom. They draw comparisons between where they live and other non-European countries and develop an awareness of the world’s climate, increasing their understanding of the world and their place in it.
View Curriculum Document
Design & Technology
In Design & Technology, students take part in enjoyable projects that seek to challenge them and develop their creative and technical skills. We foster their burgeoning creativity and flair for design by engaging them in various aspects of production: our students learn to conduct background research, review criteria for design, plan and create prototypes, develop their practical skills, and techniques, and finally evaluate the finished product. Years 1 and 2 also involve learning to model new ideas, describe the purpose of different products, create with a range of tools and materials, follow safety and hygiene procedures, make simple judgements about their products and suggest improvements.
View Curriculum Document
PSHE
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education is critical for promoting our students’ continued welfare, and for helping them flourish both in school and beyond. Through a varied and engaging curriculum, children learn how to live in the wider world, gain strong relationship skills and look after their health and wellbeing. PSHE lessons aim to instil courage, resilience, core values and a positive outlook; we also teach students to understand issues like the importance of humour, relationships, emotions and the ingredients for success, as well as bullying and how to tackle it.
Relationships & Health Education (RHE) is part of the PSHE syllabus and likewise aims to promote pupils’ wellbeing. We encourage all students to learn the value of respect, love, care, self-respect and empathy for others, in the context of trusting, stable and loving relationships. In Key Stage 1, students learn about how animals (including humans) move, feed, grow and reproduce, as well as the main parts of the body.
Opportunities outside the classroom help students to develop a sense of the value of money, including ‘real-life’ scenarios, like a toy sale, the school fair and charity initiatives. We take mental wellbeing very seriously both in PSHE and throughout school life; for this reason, we have a dedicated Mental Wellbeing Lead whose role is to work with members of the school community to promote children’s wellbeing.
View Curriculum Document
Religious Education
At Chepstow House, we recognise that learning about, and promoting respect and tolerance for, different faiths is very important; this view is reflected in our school's Religious Education syllabus. Our enriching curriculum aims to expose students to various faiths and explore the differences and similarities between them. In addition, students in years 1 and 2 have the opportunity to visit a place of worship.
View Curriculum Document
Throughout Key Stage 1, children attend specialist lessons to develop a deeper understanding of a range of topics. From performing arts sessions that teach physical control and problem-solving to establishing lifelong language skills in French classes, our pupils enjoy various opportunities to discover and cultivate their unique talents. Lessons are taught by specialist teachers who, by sharing their passion for the subject, inspire children to explore their curiosity, garner critical thinking skills, and develop the tools needed to succeed in school and beyond.
Specialist subjects in Key Stage 1 include Art, Drama, French, Music and Physical Education (PE). For more information, please visit Our Specialist Subjects.

Key Stage 2 Curriculum
Holistic Education from Years 3 to 6
Children in years 3 to 6 follow a broad curriculum that fosters in-depth knowledge across disciplines. This is achieved by offering a broad and balanced curriculum that follows the National Curriculum and ensures children are prepared for the range of 11+ and 13+ assessments in year 6. Specialists work closely with children to develop their unique talents in Art, Music, Science and other subjects, and help them become confident, well-rounded and independent individuals.
Click on the icons below to learn more.
English
The English curriculum promotes core competencies that are essential for linguistic development, including grammar, handwriting, spelling and comprehension. Children hone their abilities during explicit lessons and various activities throughout the school week.
Opportunities for speaking and listening are provided to build confidence in communicating, such as year group and key stage debates, assemblies, spelling competitions, and presentations for parents.
Our aim is for all children to develop a love of reading. Guided reading occurs daily in class and is set for homework, and children are encouraged to read books independently.
Mathematics
Each term in Mathematics, students explore new concepts and review topics already covered to increase understanding.
The concepts covered at this stage include number and place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, fractions, decimals, percentages, measurement and geometry (including position, direction, properties of shapes, statistics and problem-solving). Ratios, proportions and algebra are introduced in years 5 and 6.
To encourage assimilation of key topics, lessons include written and practical activities, and we use Numicon to support number understanding. Careful planning helps children to advance at a pace suitable to their development.
Digital Literacy
Digital Literacy & Computing
Chepstow House students gain some of the most in-demand skills in the 21st century; these include digital literacy, which helps children use modern technologies in ways that can lead to outstanding results in class and beyond. The computing curriculum is both varied and flexible to make room for new technologies; thus, we ensure students stay at the forefront of relevant developments in the digital world.
Building on lessons from previous years, Key Stage 2 students become increasingly adept in the use of digital technology, including in coding, Microsoft Office software, and various creative and collaborative tools. In structured computing lessons and across the curriculum, we teach students about a range of core concepts, such as e-safety, online communication, the production of digital content (which includes the use of text, image, sound and animation software), data and computational thinking.
In digital literacy as in other areas, we take safety very seriously. Using technology in safe, respectful and responsible ways is a common theme throughout Chepstow House. In addition, we use Microsoft SharePoint and Teams for linking work in class with homework as well as for celebrating our students’ accomplishments.
Humanities
Our engaging humanities curriculum helps children to develop their knowledge and understanding of the world by employing a range of skills linked to history and geography. Focal points in the geography syllabus include: places, locations and patterns; environmental change and other processes; and the concept of sustainable development. In history lessons, we encourage our students to consider historical events, their causes and consequences, and compare ways of life in different time periods. As a result, children grow knowledgeable on various topics, such as Pre-Roman Britain, the Vikings and Early Civilisations, and explore case studies involving local and recent British history, such as The Battle of Britain.
Design & Technology
Design & Technology lessons provide students with a vibrant, dynamic environment in which to develop their creative skills and become budding designers. Through exciting, project-based work, they learn to undertake background research, review design criteria, devise and produce product prototypes, apply practical skills and techniques to create finished products and finally assess their work. In years 3 to 6, we challenge them to describe the purpose of products, create a design specification, model ideas using prototypes and patterns, utilise a range of tools and materials, follow safety and hygiene procedures, apply various finishing techniques and critically evaluate the quality of their work, including design and manufacture.
PSHE
Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education
A strong focus on Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education is integral to the welfare of each student and serves as a critical foundation for success in later life. Through a carefully planned PSHE syllabus, we teach students how to flourish in the wider world, build positive relationships and maintain their health and wellbeing.
At the heart of PSHE lessons is the promotion of courage, resilience, core values and an understanding of emotions, relationships, and the ingredients for success. We give children the opportunity to explore different attitudes, values and beliefs, and to develop the skills and strategies to manage issues that may arise in their lives. We also cover bullying and how to tackle it.
We also provide lessons in Relationships & Health Education (RHE) as part of the PSHE curriculum to instruct students in the value of respect, love, care, self-respect and empathy – in the context of trusting, stable and loving relationships – at appropriate age levels. Years 3 and 4 cover stereotypes, positive relationships and the main differences between boys and girls (including an overview of body parts), and the difference between acceptable and unacceptable physical contact. Explicit Relationships and Sex Education lessons take place in years 5 and 6, and teach students about physical development, including puberty (years 5 and 6) and reproduction (year 6), in addition to managing their emotions.
Outside the classroom, children enjoy opportunities to learn the value of money, including real-life scenarios like the school fair and charity fundraising events. Mental wellbeing is taken very seriously at Chepstow House – in PSHE as well as throughout school life. To promote children’s wellbeing, our Mental Wellbeing Lead works closely with all members of the school community.
Religious Education
Respect and tolerance for different faiths are integral to our school’s value system, and are firmly embedded in our Religious Education syllabus. In Key Stage 2, children continue to build upon previous years' learnings by extending their knowledge and understanding of world religions. Our broad syllabus ensures pupils become knowledgeable about a wide variety of subjects, such as: beliefs and values; the significance of key leaders; worship and sacred places; religious symbols and expression; celebrations and festivals; inspirational people; and religion, family and community.
Reasoning
Explicit Reasoning lessons help children to develop a deeper understanding of the strategies that they can use when solving a variety of challenges. By participating in verbal, non-verbal and spatial activities, our students gain numerous skills related to reasoning, such as justifying their approaches, providing clear verbal explanations and solving written challenges both on paper and online. Our cross-curricular approach aims to improve students’ outcomes across disciplines by linking reasoning to other subject areas – for example, our development of language in English or spatial awareness in Design & Technology.
Specialist lessons continue throughout Key Stage 2, helping children become confident, multi-skilled individuals. From utilising video and editing technology to record drama performances to investigating scientific topics, children develop a range of competencies to apply in class and out. While deepening their knowledge across subject areas, children learn to think deeply and critically, as well as cultivating their unique interests.
Specialist subjects in Key Stage 2 include Science, French, Music, Art, Drama and Physical Education (PE). For more information, please visit Our Specialist Subjects.

Our Safeguarding
Our Safeguarding
At Chepstow House, the safeguarding of our children is the highest priority. Safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children is everyone’s responsibility at Chepstow House School. In order to fulfil this responsibility effectively, all professionals should make sure their approach is child centred.
The list below shows the safeguarding team within school.

When recruiting we follow the safer recruitment practice. All interviewing staff have been trained on safer recruitment. These practices help make sure staff and volunteers are suitable to work with children and young people. It’s a vital part of creating a safe and positive environment and making a commitment to keep children safe from harm.

Student Enrichment
Outstanding Opportunities for All-Rounded Development
Chepstow House pupils enjoy opportunities to extend learning outside of traditional academia, with enrichment initiatives designed to maximise the potential of each child. We provide invaluable experiences that foster the unique talents and social skills of each pupil, including leadership, resilience and independence, which will benefit them in senior school and beyond.
House System
Throughout school life, children’s accomplishments are recognised and celebrated. Our house system promotes excellence by rewarding achievements in areas such as academia, sports, and the arts.
Upon joining Chepstow House, children are placed in one of four houses. The houses compete with each other for house points, which are awarded based on members' accomplishments. Pupils are motivated to excel both in class and at events such as galas, debates, and spelling competitions. The breadth of activities for which points are awarded means that all children can participate.
School Council
Joining the School Council is a fantastic opportunity to develop key skills for school and later life, including teamwork, leadership and problem-solving. Children consider important issues in school life. Children work together with other representatives to initiate plans and present solutions. Examples of previous initiatives include helping to design the school lunch menu, introducing new clubs, and establishing a playground buddy system.
At the beginning of each term, every class elects their School Council representative. Meetings are held every half term and are chaired by our Year 6 leaders. Minutes from meetings are recorded and distributed to each class and the Senior Leadership Team for discussion.
Responsibilities
In addition to School Council, older pupils also have the opportunity to take on further responsibilities. Our Head and Deputy Head Boys and Girls, and Sport and House Captains, develop leadership skills in their roles while representing our broad school community. Other children take up roles that foster organisational skills and awareness of specific subjects, such as our Junior Travel Ambassadors, who promote active road safety through talks and surveys, and contribute to the school travel plan.
Eco Warriors
Chepstow House is a proud advocate of youth-led environmental action and education, and holds the coveted Eco-Schools Green Flag accreditation. If elected to our school’s Eco Committee, children address relevant environmental issues that require them to develop their problem-solving, communication and organisational skills – all of which are applicable in other areas of life. Witnessing the projects they have worked on being realised is a profound experience that builds confidence and inspires the children to become changemakers in the school and community.
The Eco Committee meet every half term to discuss their initiatives and progress. Though the agenda is set by the children, visitors are often invited to join and offer their expertise. Each year, the committee carry out an environmental review to evaluate the school’s strengths and weaknesses, then create an action plan with targets for the upcoming year.
Diversity Council
As members of the Diversity Council, children can contribute to the positive development of our rich school community. Children expand their knowledge and understanding of diversity by championing important initiatives, such as the promotion of equal opportunities and supporting diversity education in our school curriculum. Collaboration and teamwork are encouraged, as the children have to engage with other Diversity Council members, including pupils, staff and parents.
Charities
When children are taught about charitable giving, they learn how to take care of others, be respectful, and develop empathy, kindness and compassion. Through our active, ongoing support for local and global charities, Chepstow House not only bolsters these worthy causes but also promotes pupils’ awareness and understanding of the wider world.
As part of our giving efforts, we introduce learners to a range of public institutions and services in England and their local community. In addition, fundraising events for both parents and pupils take place throughout the school year.
For details of the charities we support, please visit Giving Back.
Discover more about our enrichment initiatives and how your child can benefit from these excellent opportunities.
